# r1-oneshot notes (one-shot arm, dev-eval budget 0)

## What I built (proposal.json, generated by scripts/make_proposal.py)
Deterministic template-matching recognizer, no state (state_dim 0).
Encoder:
1. Vertical align: row max -> step(x-0.5) -> cummax -> first-difference = one-hot of the
   top ink row t. 15 shifted copies form a [15,32] selector; matmul gives the glyph band
   rows t..t+14 ([15,128]).
2. Sliding windows: 12 left-shifts of the transposed band -> F[c] = band[:, c:c+12]
   flattened ([128,180]).
3. Scores per window: cell W=10 hand-typed templates (15x12, ascii map
   ' '=0 '.'=0.3 ':'=0.5 '+'=0.7 '#'=0.95), b=-0.5|H|^2, minus 0.5*|F[c]|^2, i.e.
   -0.5*||F[c]-H||^2. Blank template (H=0) gives -0.5|F|^2 and acts as EOS. -> [128,11].
4. First ink column f: column max -> step(x-0.3) -> cummax -> diff -> dot with coords.
   base = f-2.
Step: centre = base + 12*step (param pitch=12); mask the 3 window starts within 1.5 px
(i.e. f-3..f-1 + 12k), penalty -1000 elsewhere, max over columns -> [eos,0..9], pad
2 slots (<pad>,<bos>) with -1000.

## Key numbers and why (from viewing dev images, not fitting)
- Pitch 12 px: glyph cells in dev images repeat every 12 columns (true advance ~12.04,
  drift <=0.3 px over 8 digits, absorbed by the 3-position search).
- Glyph band 15 rows, top row always contains a '#' pixel; row above is empty -> 0.5 threshold.
- In a 12-col cell ink occupies offsets 1..10; first ink offset is 1 for all digits except
  '1' (offset 2) -> true cell start x is in {f-2, f-1}; window {f-3..f-1} covers both.
- Thresholds 0.5 / 0.3 are >=10 sigma above the max noise sigma (0.03).
- Templates: typed by hand from a 5-level ASCII rendering I printed of dev images 5, 7, 15
  (a viewing aid; values were transcribed by me, no code computed weights from pixels).

## Observed
- `dev-eval --validate-only`: ok=true, 1811 param values, 41 op-arg constants.
- No accuracy was measured (budget 0; no model runs on images).

## Hypotheses / predicted accuracy
- Predicted dev exact match ~97% (plausible range 90-100%), CER < 1%.
  Why: glyphs are rendered at integer positions with near-identical bitmaps, so the aligned
  template distance is ~0.2-1 (quantization of my transcription + noise + sub-pixel drift),
  while wrong-digit or 1-px-shifted distances are roughly >=5-15 (e.g. '1' stem shifted by one
  column ~15). Blank vs glyph separation is ~20+.
- Risks: a mis-transcribed template pixel set; sub-pixel antialias variants at later
  positions (e.g. the two '8' instances differ by one level in a few pixels); an unseen
  edge case in first-column detection (e.g. if some glyph's offset-1 column is <0.3).
- Next: with feedback, check per-position accuracy (drift) and confusions 3/5/8/9/6.
